description:
MEASURED AND FIXED 2026-08-12 in crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop.

RELATED TO op-289n but NOT the same defect. op-289n records that TampinesSteamArray::set_inlet_enthalpy has no effect at all, and cites OPCPFluidArray as the healthy reference. Independent reproduction shows OPCP was NOT healthy either -- it merely LOOKED healthy because the reporting driver re-issued set_inlet_enthalpy() every step.

SYMPTOM. FvMatrix::solve builds its output VolScalarField with zero-gradient boundaries. step() captured and re-stamped the BC templates for u (correct_bcs_vec) and p (correct_bcs) but NOT for he, so 'self.he = he_new' after the energy solve silently discarded every prescribed enthalpy boundary. set_inlet_enthalpy therefore took effect on the first outer corrector after the call and never again.

MEASUREMENT (Nitrogen, 8 cells, 1 m, 1e-4 m2, 1 bar, PISO 2 correctors, dt 2e-4 s, inlet velocity 0.5 m/s, outlet p 1 bar; uniform seed differing from the inlet BC; BC applied ONCE).
  seed 300 K (h 311.20 kJ/kg), inlet BC 520.45 kJ/kg:
    pre-fix,  2000 steps: he[0] = 311.48 kJ/kg  (0.13 % of the 209.25 kJ/kg gap)
    pre-fix, 10000 steps: no cell more than 0.4 kJ/kg from the seed
    post-fix, 3000 steps: he[0] = 556.52 kJ/kg (117.2 % of gap), field mean 364.98 kJ/kg
  seed 500 K (h 520.45 kJ/kg), inlet BC 311.20 kJ/kg:
    pre-fix,  2000 steps: he[0] = 520.16 kJ/kg  (0.14 % of gap)
    post-fix, 3000 steps: he[0] = 296.13 kJ/kg (107.2 % of gap), field mean 444.68 kJ/kg
Post-fix, a run that re-applies the BC every step is bit-identical to one that applies it once -- so no existing caller's numbers move.

FIX. rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs step(): capture he's BC template alongside u's and p's, and correct_bcs(&mut he_new, &he_bcs) after the energy solve.

REGRESSION TESTS (both directions, uniform field differing from the BC, BC applied once -- the blind spot op-289n identifies):
  lateral_coupling::tests::inlet_enthalpy_bc_heats_uniform_field_without_reapplying_each_step
  lateral_coupling::tests::inlet_enthalpy_bc_cools_uniform_field_without_reapplying_each_step

COORDINATION. tampines-steam-tables carries the same missing he BC re-stamp in its own step(); whoever fixes op-289n should apply the same capture/re-stamp there. It is probably NOT the whole story on that side: OPCP responded correctly to a per-step re-issue and TampinesSteamArray reportedly does not, so tampines has at least one further defect.
title: OPCPFluidArray: set_inlet_enthalpy was a one-shot -- the energy solve discarded the BC (FIXED)

description:
MAINTAINER REQUEST 2026-08-11: "I think there should be a good interface for me to make notes via kovan." Filed for a later session, not started.

THE NEED. The archive now holds 16 documents and is growing fast — five HTR-10 papers arrived in a single morning. Reading them produces exactly the kind of knowledge that currently has nowhere to live: which figure holds the LOFC transient, which table the correlation came from, why one paper contradicts another, what a number actually means in context. Today that ends up in commit messages, bead comments, or nowhere at all.

WHAT IT SHOULD PROBABLY DO — for the maintainer to shape, these are candidates not requirements:
- Notes ATTACHED to a KovanDocument, not floating in a separate file, so a note cannot outlive or drift from the document it is about.
- Anchored where possible: page, section, figure or table number. A note saying "the 1046.6 C figure is at 120 percent overload, not nominal" is worth far more when it points at the page.
- Cross-document links, since the interesting knowledge is comparative. Real example from 2026-08-11: HTR-10 own fuel temperature LIMIT is 1230 C per Gao and Shi, while the 1600 C that pervades the modular-HTR literature including kugeler2017vhtr is the GENERIC coated-particle retention limit. Conflating them would misstate a safety margin, and that distinction currently survives only in a bead comment.
- Links out to beads and to source files, mirroring what CATALOGUE.md already does by hand.
- Notes are the maintainer own voice and should be distinguishable from extracted document text — never silently merged into the markdown body.

INTERFACE. The TUI is the natural home (kovan-tui, or the digitiser TUI pattern from op-5v5.8), since note-taking is a human activity and the CLI is the agent path. A CLI verb for appending a note non-interactively is still worth having so an agent can record a finding for the maintainer to review.

RESPECT THE EXISTING GRAIN:
- Notes on a PROPRIETARY document must stay gitignored with it. A note quoting a paywalled paper at length inherits its restrictions.
- huang2025waterIngress is a special case: its full text is deliberately not extracted because of a TDM/AI reservation (op-b7bx). Notes on it are the maintainer OWN words about it, which is fine and arguably the whole point — but the tooling must not use notes as a back door to reconstructing the text.
- Provenance discipline as everywhere else: who wrote the note and when.

RELATED: op-5v5.8 (graph digitiser, whose review workflow already records who verified what and when — the same pattern), and the KovanDocument model in kovan-common, which is the source of truth and would need a notes field or a sidecar.
title: kovan: a note-taking interface over catalogued documents

description: Extend refine_near_boundary to a max_level parameter: refine the near-surface band progressively to max_level (each level refines the boundary leaves of the previous), then run a 2:1 BALANCING pass (refine any leaf coarser than a face-neighbour by >1 level) so level differences are <=1 everywhere and the hanging-node face split stays valid. build_mesh parameterized by max_level (finest resolution base/2^max_level). V&V: box refined to max_level 2 keeps EXACT volume, validate closed (incl polyhedra), more cells than 1-level, level differences <=1; max_level 1 reproduces the prior 456-cell result.
title: cfmesh: multi-level octree refinement + 2:1 balancing

description: MeshNeutronics (multi_region/mesh_region.rs) currently drives DiffusionNeutronics with a GLOBAL Doppler feedback: it collapses the mapped TFuel field to one importance-weighted mean temperature and re-materialises the whole-mesh cross sections at that single point (DiffusionXsFields::materialize takes one feedback vector for all cells). Two neutronics-subtree API additions would lift this to full fidelity: (1) a materialize variant accepting a PER-CELL parameter array so each cell's XS use its local temperature (upstream setNeutronicsVariables.H evaluates per cell); (2) a public DiffusionNeutronics::set_k_eff / dynamic-reactivity setter so a scalar Delta-rho from the ReactivityFeedback layer can be injected into a diffusion TRANSIENT step (step() currently reads k_eff only from solve_eigenvalue; there is no public mutator, so the mesh path demonstrates negative feedback via steady eigenvalue re-solves, not a dynamic transient reactivity insertion). Both are edits to crate::genfoam::neutronics (owned by the neutronics fleet), out of scope for the multi_region subtree. Until then the global-feedback + steady path is real and closes the loop (V&V in mesh_region.rs tests).
title: genfoam multiRegion: per-cell / dynamic mesh XS feedback (neutronics-subtree API gap)

description:
Deferred by the maintainer 2026-08-04 after several rounds of on-screen iteration. The turbine looks acceptable; the blade LEAN convention is not settled and should be decided against a proper reference rather than by eye.

WHAT IS SETTLED (do not redo):
  - Blade HEIGHT mirrors about the admission plane for double flow. Enforced by the test double_flow_geometry_is_symmetric_about_the_admission_plane. The rotor radius must blend from the LESS-EXPANDED neighbour (nearer admission), not from row+1 -- +x is downstream on one half and upstream on the other, and blending toward row+1 on both halves broke the symmetry.
  - Blades are rooted at the hub, run radially to the tip, and project root and tip by the same cos(phi) so they shorten onto the shaft edge-on.
  - Blades are cambered quadratic Beziers; camber runs in OPPOSITE senses for stator and rotor. That opposition is what turns the flow and extracts work.
  - The stator ring is drawn whole; only the ROTOR hides its far half (that is what reads as rotation).

WHAT IS NOT SETTLED -- the lean (overall slant), as distinct from the camber:
  - Attempt 1: lean applied in a fixed x direction. Maintainer: rotor blades not symmetric.
  - Attempt 2: lean mirrored with flow direction via a flow_sign helper. Maintainer: stator wrong on the left, rotor wrong on the right. Those four observations are only satisfiable by uniform lean with the rotor base inverted, so flow_sign was removed.
  - Attempt 3 (current): lean uniform across the machine; stator negative (angles down, maintainer-verified for SINGLE flow), rotor negative. Consequence: the two rows now lean the SAME way, and only the camber opposes.

OPEN QUESTIONS:
  1. Should lean mirror with flow direction on a double-flow machine, or stay uniform because the shaft turns one way along its whole length? Physical argument exists both ways: mirrored blades are what cancel axial thrust in a double-flow rotor, but rotation sense is common.
  2. Is it right that stator and rotor lean the same way and only the camber opposes?
  3. Double flow has NOT been re-checked since the stator lean was flipped on 2026-08-04; the earlier 'stator looks right on the right half' judgement predates that flip.

HOW TO SETTLE IT: against a published turbine velocity-triangle / blade-profile reference, not by eye. Anything adopted must be documented with its source per the workspace provenance rule. Note the angles themselves are still placeholders (op-wqk.14.11) and become real when the physical turbine model lands (op-dt3.18) -- it may be cheapest to settle lean and angles together at that point.
title: TurbineVisual: settle stator/rotor blade lean direction (deferred)
